findings.quote: but were disputing over Sardinia and Sicily as well, and were trying to grasp everything
findings.problem: Greek has a marked gap: ἠμφισβήτουν:... καὶ πάντα περιελάμβανον. The English reads straight on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: but were disputing over Sardinia and Sicily as well [text lost here] ... and were trying to grasp everything

units.note: Rest of chapter checked: Gnaeus (land) and Publius (fleet) in Iberia, Marcus Valerius then Publius Sulpicius, Appius with 100 quinqueremes, Marcus Claudius, Hamilcar all match.
Numbers (sixty quinqueremes, eight, four-foot ladder, four men, three sides) all match.

Ten talents matches. Chapter ends mid-sentence in Greek (ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν ναῦν) and the English completes it with the opening of ch. 6 (καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κινδυνεύειν ὁλοσχερῶς); that is a chapter seam, not a smoothed lacuna.

findings.quote: watching from within the city his own assaults beaten off with loss to himself and laughter from the defenders
findings.problem: Greek: θεωρῶν μετὰ βλάβης καὶ χλευασμοῦ τοὺς ἔνδον ἀποτριβομένους αὑτοῦ τὰς ἐπιβολάς. τοὺς ἔνδον are the men inside (the defenders), who are warding off his plans. Marcus is not within the city.
findings.proposed_fix: seeing the men inside parry his attempts, to his own loss and mockery

findings.quote: Archimedes was ladling the sea out of his ships
findings.problem: Greek: ταῖς μὲν ναυσὶν αὐτοῦ κυαθίζειν ἐκ θαλάττης Ἀρχιμήδη. Archimedes uses Marcus's ships as ladles (κύαθοι) to draw water from the sea. The English reverses this by making the ships the source the sea is ladled out of.
findings.proposed_fix: Archimedes was using his ships as ladles to dip water out of the sea

units.note: ἔκσπονδοι (sambucae thrown out disgracefully like those excluded from the libations) is a rendering choice, left alone.
Eight months, two parts and a third all match.

findings.quote: Demetrius, after rashly and recklessly attempting
findings.problem: Greek opens with a fragment and a gap: καταλαβέσθαι... ἐγχειρήσας. No subject is preserved in the text; Demetrius comes only from the editor's footnote (cf. Polyb. III 19, 11). The English presents it as a complete sentence with a stated subject.
findings.proposed_fix: [Demetrius (name supplied by the editor; the opening of the sentence is lost)] ... having rashly and recklessly attempted

units.note: Remainder (with Philip's consent, seize the city of the Messenians, killed at the moment of action, details to come) matches.
